A physical description, medical history, professional background, a list of hobbies/interests, a childhood picture of the donor etc. Some donors are open to being contacted when the child is an adult. I wanted to find a donor open to this but I was not able to. I chose my donor because he matched all of the other requirements relating to health and was from the same ethnic background as me. That sounds bad, but I feel a strong connection to my home country even though I no longer live there, and it was important to me that my child be the same ethnicity. I was talking to a friend about it this weekend and I mentioned that I was thinking of typing up something 'from' the donor that was a little more encouraging or at least a little longer. I wouldn't change the essence of the note but I would expand on it so it didn't feel so half-assed. I feel terrible for my child. I know I'll provide all the love and stability in the world but there will come a time when they will wonder. I'm not sure what to do, but my friend advised me that I'm overly emotional at the moment due to hormones and it wouldn't be fair to fake the note even if my child will never find out. I think she's probably right but I'm tempted to give my child more than they've been offered here. WIBTA?

| What you’re doing | Why it matters | How it can boost your day |

| **Personal routine** | Routines create predictability, which can lower anxiety and improve time management. | You’re less likely to skip other important tasks because you’ve already “checked off” a key part of your morning. |

### A few ways to keep the momentum going

3. **Reflect on the impact** – At the end of the week, jot down how you felt before and after your grooming routine. You might notice patterns that reinforce its value.

- How long does your shaving/trimming routine usually take?
- Do you notice any changes in how you handle the day’s first tasks after you’re done?
- Is there anything you’d like to tweak—maybe a different product or a slightly different routine—to make it even more effective?
